preparation_representation: A material word denotes the declared base plus its ordered preparation history, read as the already stated left-to-right suffix sequence. A bare base has the empty history. forbid_match: FORBID(base,F) bars subsequent ADD(base,A) in its written scope exactly when F is a prefix of A. Base identity is the shared canonical identity just specified. Thus a bare-base prohibition bars every preparation descendant of that base. A prohibition on DRIED(base) also bars GROUND(DRIED(base)); it does not automatically bar DRIED(GROUND(base)), whose declared history starts differently. This limited provenance-based prohibition, including its order sensitivity, must be what the author intends. A source demanding broader chemical or all-history exclusion lies outside the domain unless expressed as the corresponding explicitly enumerated base/history prohibitions.
